$comment: FHWA Scheme F classes 8-10. Tractor-semitrailer combinations.
HOW THE LONGITUDINAL SPACINGS WERE SET
Intra-group spacings are the AASHTOWare Pavement ME defaults (tandem
51.6 in = 1311 mm, tridem 49.2 in = 1250 mm). Tractor wheelbases are the
Pavement ME wheelbase classes (short 12 ft, medium 15 ft, long 18 ft).
The distance from the drive group to the trailer group is NOT a free
choice: it is set to the smallest realistic value at which the vehicle
satisfies the Federal Bridge Formula at its stated legal loads,
checked over EVERY axle subset, not merely the outer bridge. That gives
these layouts a reproducible engineering basis rather than an eyeballed
one. test/run.mjs re-derives the check and fails if any subset violates it.

Track 1829 mm (72 in) is the classic dual-wheel spacing of the flexible-pavement literature (Yoder & Witczak; Huang). Dual spacing 330 mm (13 in) — see data/SOURCES.md for the 12-13.5 in range across sources.

load.basis: 17 000 lb — half of the 34 000 lb federal tandem-axle limit (23 CFR 658.17).

axles.source: Trailer tandem position is governed by the Federal Bridge Formula, not by styling. The binding subset is A2-A5, four axles carrying 68 000 lb, which the formula allows only over a spread of 11 887 mm (39.0 ft) or more; the tandem is set slightly beyond that at 12 025 mm (39.4 ft) so the vehicle clears the limit with margin rather than sitting exactly on it. With the group spacing at 1311 mm this places A4 at 16 200 mm. Kingpin-to-rear-axle is then about 11 400 mm (37 ft), within the 40 ft limit applied by states that regulate KPRA.

load.basis: 17 000 lb — half of the 34 000 lb federal tandem-axle limit (23 CFR 658.17).

axles.source: 1311 mm behind A4 — the AASHTOWare Pavement ME default tandem axle spacing of 51.6 in. Outer bridge A1-A5 is then 17 511 mm (57.5 ft), comfortably above the 51.2 ft the bridge formula requires for 80 000 lb on five axles.

axleGroups.source: AASHTOWare Pavement ME Design default tandem axle spacing, 51.6 in = 1310.6 mm, rounded to 1311 mm. Verified during this build.

gvw.basis: 80 000 lb — the US federal gross vehicle weight limit (23 CFR 658.17), distributed in the canonical 12 000 / 34 000 / 34 000 lb split.

units.notes: The reference vehicle of US pavement engineering: a five-axle tractor-semitrailer at the 80 000 lb legal gross with the 12/34/34 axle split. This unit is covered by a dedicated regression test that pins its axle positions, track widths and dual spacings, and independently re-derives Federal Bridge Formula compliance over every axle subset.
